+
+---
+authors: Chris Clark (cclark.0804@gmail.com)
+state: draft
+---
+
+# RFD 0 - RFDs
+
+## What
+
+Implement a prototype job worker service that provides an API to run arbitrary Linux processes.
+
+The project is broken down into 3 components:
+
+- A reusable library implementing the functionality for working with jobs.
+- An API server that wraps the functionality of the library.
+- A command line interface (CLI) that communicates with the API server.
+
+Additionally, it needs to meet the level 4 requirements. 
+### Library
+- Worker library with methods to start/stop/query status and get the output of a job.
+- Library should be able to stream the output of a running job.
+- Output should be from start of process execution.
+- Multiple concurrent clients should be supported.
+- Add resource control for CPU, Memory and Disk IO per job using cgroups.
+###API
+- GRPC API to start/stop/get status/stream output of a running process.
+- Use mTLS authentication and verify client certificate. Set up strong set of cipher suites for TLS and good crypto setup for certificates. Do not use any other authentication protocols on top of mTLS.
+- Use a simple authorization scheme.
+### Client
+- CLI should be able to connect to worker service and start, stop, get status, and stream output of a job.
+
+## Why
+
+The purpose of this proposal is to display the candidate's ability as a golang software developer. 
+It will display the candidate's ability to design and implement a simple gRPC client CLI and server that 
+communicates using mTLS for authentication and simple authorization scheme.  
+
+### Job State
+The server will store job state and output into tmp plain txt files. This is a simple way to persist job 
+details and support multiple clients and avoid complexity of using a database as a dependency.  Ideally, 
+I'd implement data schema using mongodb as it will be easier to maintain for long term use and offload 
+ttl logic to the database.  
+### Server
+Server will be implement the gRPC api and responsible for knowing how to start, stop, and query jobs requested
+by the client.  It will also enforce mTLS for authentication and a simple authorization scheme. 
+
+### CLI
+Simple CLI schema that implements client side mTLS for authentication to meet the requirements of the 
+project.  It will be able to submit gRPC requests to the server and stream the output to stdout.  
+
+### mTLS
+Hardcoded certificate files will be used for the client and server certificates will be used for 
+simplicity sakes and to demonstrate the ability to use mTLS and the simple authorization schema. This is 
+not a secure implementation.  the use of a proxy middleware or separate library that can issue certificates
+and maintain the certificates and client permissions would be more ideal to meet security concerns. 
+
+### cgroups
+The arbitrary linux processes ran by the server will need to have limited resources available to them as to 
+not allow any one process to hog all the resources of the server.  
+
+## Details
+### Proto
+The protp file is simple. Defines a service with simple `StartJob`, `StopJob`, and `FetchJob` methods. Where
+starting and fetching a job will stream the output to the client. 
+```azure
+
+service V1 {
+
+  // Start job that will run a linux process and return stream of metadata
+  // about job and output.
+  rpc StartJob (StartJobReq) returns (stream JobResp) {};
+
+// Stop a running job keyed by the job id.
+  rpc StopJob (StopJobReq) returns (StopJobResp) {};
+
+// Fetch running our archived job metadata and output.  Jobs metadata and
+  // output are written to tmp files for temporary storage and can be retrieved
+  // by the server to return to multiple clients without affecting other
+  // clients.
+  rpc FetchJob(FetchJobReq) returns (stream JobResp) {};
+}
+
+enum Status {
+  STATUS_RUNNING = 0;
+STATUS_STOPPED = 1;
+STATUS_ERROR = 2;
+}
+
+message StopJobResp {
+  Status Status = 1;
+}
+
+message JobResp {
+  // UUID ID of job. 
+  string ID = 1;
+// PID of the process running. 
+  string PID = 2;
+// Job Status. 
+  Status status = 3;
+// Job output. 
+  string Output = 4;
+}

+### Client
+- CLI should be able to connect to worker service and start, stop, get status, and stream output of a job.
+

+
+The purpose of this proposal is to display the candidate's ability as a golang software developer. 
+It will display the candidate's ability to design and implement a simple gRPC client CLI and server that 
+communicates using mTLS for authentication and simple authorization scheme.  
+
+### Job State
+The server will store job state and output into tmp plain txt files. This is a simple way to persist job 
+details and support multiple clients and avoid complexity of using a database as a dependency.  Ideally, 
+I'd implement data schema using mongodb as it will be easier to maintain for long term use and offload 
+ttl logic to the database.  
+### Server
+Server will be implement the gRPC api and responsible for knowing how to start, stop, and query jobs requested
+by the client.  It will also enforce mTLS for authentication and a simple authorization scheme. 
+
+### CLI
+Simple CLI schema that implements client side mTLS for authentication to meet the requirements of the

+
+### mTLS
+Hardcoded certificate files will be used for the client and server certificates will be used for 
+simplicity sakes and to demonstrate the ability to use mTLS and the simple authorization schema. This is 
+not a secure implementation.  the use of a proxy middleware or separate library that can issue certificates
+and maintain the certificates and client permissions would be more ideal to meet security concerns. 
+

+The arbitrary linux processes ran by the server will need to have limited resources available to them as to 
+not allow any one process to hog all the resources of the server.  
+

+### Proto
+The protp file is simple. Defines a service with simple `StartJob`, `StopJob`, and `FetchJob` methods. Where
+starting and fetching a job will stream the output to the client. 
+```azure
+
+service V1 {
+
+  // Start job that will run a linux process and return stream of metadata
+  // about job and output.
+  rpc StartJob (StartJobReq) returns (stream JobResp) {};
+
+// Stop a running job keyed by the job id.
+  rpc StopJob (StopJobReq) returns (StopJobResp) {};
+
+// Fetch running our archived job metadata and output.  Jobs metadata and
+  // output are written to tmp files for temporary storage and can be retrieved
+  // by the server to return to multiple clients without affecting other
+  // clients.
+  rpc FetchJob(FetchJobReq) returns (stream JobResp) {};
+}
+
+enum Status {
+  STATUS_RUNNING = 0;
+STATUS_STOPPED = 1;
+STATUS_ERROR = 2;
+}
+
+message StopJobResp {
+  Status Status = 1;
+}
+
+message JobResp {
+  // UUID ID of job. 
+  string ID = 1;
+// PID of the process running. 
+  string PID = 2;
+// Job Status. 
+  Status status = 3;
+// Job output. 
+  string Output = 4;
+}
+
+
+message StartJobReq {
+    // Linux process to be ran and its arguments. e.g. `ls`, `cd`, `echo "Hello World!"
+    string cmd = 1;
+}
+
+message StopJobReq {
+  // The uuid of the job to be stopped.
+  string id = 1;
+}

+```func StopJob(id string) error ```

+FetchJob attempts to fetch the job by ID.  Job metadata and output 
+are stored in `/tmp/` directory with the file name `$id.txt`.  If 
+job is not found it returns a not found error. 
+```func FetchJob(id stringm w io.Writer) error```
